source.title: Entropy-SGD optimizes the prior of a PAC-Bayes bound: Generalization properties of Entropy-SGD and data-dependent priors

record.tranche_reason: The study trains SGD, SGLD, Entropy-SGD and Entropy-SGLD and reports training classification error on true and random labels, bearing on whether training reaches near-zero error. The training recipes differ from the claim's stated standard SGD or Adam setup.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own training-error findings. The paper also reports test errors and generalization bounds, which are not separate rows because they do not measure training classification error. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures convolutional-network training classification error on true and random labels using SGD and several noisy gradient methods. Its CIFAR-10 experiments bear on V1 under alternative training recipes; its MNIST experiments examine the same fitting behavior in another dataset. It is not an original source for V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct but incomplete. Entropy-SGD optimizes a PAC-Bayes prior using the training data, invalidating the naive bound, and can rapidly reach zero training error on random labels. Privacy-tuned Entropy-SGLD controls overfitting but learns more slowly and has worse test performance. Its reported tighter bounds remain optimistic because convergence is assumed. Large-τ CIFAR-10 runs can again fit random labels nearly perfectly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Entropy-SGD and Entropy-SGLD, as well as SGD and SGLD; experiments use two-class MNIST and CIFAR10, with bounded cross-entropy and algorithm-specific noise and privacy settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Thermal noise changes Entropy-SGD and SGLD outcomes on two-class MNIST. On CIFAR10, the generalization gap and classifier performance change with τ and γ; the reported phase transition for random labels depends on γ.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.1 says generalization bounds are similar with and without batch normalization, while removing batch normalization requires learning-rate tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization changes learning-rate tuning requirements in these SGLD experiments; comparable generalization bounds do not establish faster training or tolerance of higher learning rates.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: Training-error values are often described qualitatively or only in figures. Some reported findings concern two-class MNIST rather than CIFAR10/100. The study says its PAC-Bayes bounds are optimistic because it assumes SGLD has converged and omits the additional convergence term.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for figure-only training-error curves in Figures 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 because precise values are not stated in the text and the figure transcription does not supply recoverable values. The textual results on test error and generalization bounds were excluded because they do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Random initialization is not specified. CIFAR-100, partial label corruption, Adam, systematic model-size effects, and early stopping are not tested. The MNIST experiments extend beyond the datasets named in V1; Entropy-SGD and Entropy-SGLD extend beyond its standard SGD/Adam recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons with identity shortcuts.
Effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, and sharpness trajectories.
Controlled training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization.

missing.what: The abstract's explicit zero-training-error result for available Entropy-SGD implementations and their Gibbs classifiers. Record it separately without assigning it to every thermal-noise setting in R4.

record.verdict_notes: An absent near-zero-fitting effect under an intentionally noisy recipe supports V1's explicit qualification; it does not challenge its standard-training assertion. Generalization gaps and test errors must not be substituted for training errors. Figure-only curves already declared in rows_left_out are not repeated as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization is not stated. CIFAR-100, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not directly tested. The study tests a two-class MNIST variant and CIFAR10, not CIFAR-100.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: SGLD training on two-class MNIST with true labels at thermal noise 0.05
rows.note: The text says SGLD achieves almost zero generalization error at this noise, but does not state a numeric training error; it describes training error as part of its risk performance.
rows.check: The value confuses generalization error with training error. Section 5.2 reports relatively large risk and an almost-zero generalization gap at thermal noise 0.05, not almost-zero training error.
